% table-across-pages — one table that a page break splits, with its header repeated.
%
% longtable repeats the header row at the top of the second page, as reports do. The
% document holds one table, so the gold file holds one table with its header once:
% a reader that emits two tables, or that keeps the repeated header as a data row,
% has read the page and not the document. The small page puts the break inside the
% table, after the fifth data row.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage{longtable}
\usepackage[paperwidth=5in,paperheight=1.9in,margin=0.4in]{geometry}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}
\begin{longtable}{|l|r|}
\hline
Month & Visitors \\
\hline
\endhead
\hline
\endfoot
January & 1200 \\
February & 1350 \\
March & 2100 \\
April & 2875 \\
May & 3920 \\
June & 5410 \\
July & 6830 \\
August & 6515 \\
\end{longtable}
\end{document}
